title: Build a two-phone Pong game that talks through sound
summary: Simon Willison had Claude Code build a two-player Pong game where phones share the game through audio chirps picked up by the microphone; he says it seems to work.
agent_role: Claude Code designed and wrote the whole game, including the audio networking, from one prompt. The human tested it on two phones.
outcome: The author reports that it seems to work.
what_they_did: Simon Willison asked Claude Code, running Opus 5.5, for a two-player game like Pong. Players hold their phones close together. The phones share what is happening in the game as sounds, heard through each phone's microphone. He also asked for twists to the look and the play. The game is published as a single web page.
how_it_went: He says it seems to work.
worth_knowing: It is one simple web page with no server behind it. The only link between the two phones is sound.
prompt: Build a two-player game in a single static HTML file, played on two phones held near each other. Send the game state between the devices as audio chirps that the other phone decodes through the web microphone API, with no server. Base it on [game idea, e.g. Pong], and add graphical and gameplay twists to make it more fun. Explain your audio encoding scheme before writing the code.

curation.rationale: A surprising build from one prompt: a two-phone game that sends its game state as audio chirps through the microphone. The live tool and session are shared, but the post is very brief.
